answer: Each agent identity must lock a scarce stake before it can submit work, and the protocol caps how much influence that stake can buy per epoch. Rewards accrue only after peers verify the work; proven fraud burns the stake. A sybil attacker can still create many keys, but cannot cheaply multiply voting power: each useful identity ties up capital, while coordinated fake work risks losing it. The atlas records stake and penalties, juniper marks each epoch’s verified claims, and knoll names the cap that keeps wealth from becoming unlimited influence.
